H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H1121: a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.)
H7141: Korach, the name of two Edomites and three Israelites
H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H7521: to be pleased with; specifically, to satisfy adebt
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H7725: to turn back (hence, away) transitively or intransitively, literally or figuratively (not necessarily with the idea of return to the starting point); generally to retreat; often adverbial, again
H7622: exile, concretely, prisoners; figuratively, a former state of prosperity
H5375: to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
H5971: a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock
H3680: properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy)
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H2403: an offence (sometimes habitual sinfulness), and its penalty, occasion, sacrifice, or expiation; also (concretely) an offender
H622: to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.)
H639: properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H6565: to break up (usually figuratively), i.e. to violate, frustrate
H5973: adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English)
H5769: properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always
H599: to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged
H4900: to draw, used in a great variety of applications (including to sow, to sound, to prolong, to develop, to march, to remove, to delay, to be tall, etc.)
H1755: properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H2421: to live, whether literally or figuratively; causatively, to revive
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H7200: to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
H2617: kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty
H5414: to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)
H8085: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
H4100: properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what (including whatever, and even relatively, that which); often used with prefixes in various adverbial or conjunctive senses
H1696: perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue
H410: strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H7965: safe, i.e. (figuratively) well, happy, friendly; also (abstractly) welfare, i.e. health, prosperity, peace
H413: near, with or among; often in general, to
H408: not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing
H3690: in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness
H389: a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only
H7931: to reside or permanently stay (literally or figuratively)
H3519: properly, weight, but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness
H6298: to come in contact with, whether by accident or violence; figuratively, to concur
H6664: the right (natural, moral or legal); also (abstractly) equity or (figuratively) prosperity
H5401: to kiss, literally or figuratively (touch); also (as a mode of attachment), to equip with weapons
H6779: to sprout (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative)
H8064: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
H8259: properly, to lean out (of a window), i.e. (by implication) peep or gaze (passively, be a spectacle)
H1571: properly, assemblage; used only adverbially also, even, yea, though; often repeated as correl. both...and
H2896: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
H2981: produce, i.e. a crop or (figuratively) wealth
H6440: the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
H1980: to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
H7760: to put (used in a great variety of applications, literal, figurative, inferentially, and elliptically)
H1870: a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
H6471: a stroke, literally or figuratively (in various applications, as follow)
